title: What is Dino USB Player for Roku?
content: Dino USB Player is a Roku app for finding and playing video files from an attached USB drive. It gives you a remote-friendly USB video browser, full-screen playback, subtitles, resume support, and subscription options.

title: How do I start using the app?
content: Connect a USB storage device to your Roku device, open Dino USB Player, wait for the app to scan your drive, then choose a video from the USB browser.

title: Do I need a USB drive?
content: Yes. Dino USB Player is designed for videos stored on an external USB storage device connected to your Roku.

title: What happens if no USB drive is connected?
content: The app shows a No USB Connected state. Connect a USB drive and use Reload Files if you want the app to check again.

title: Does the app scan folders and subfolders?
content: Yes. Dino USB Player recursively scans folders and subfolders for supported video files.

title: Does the browser show folders?
content: No. The visible USB browser lists video files only. Folders are scanned in the background so videos inside subfolders can still appear.

title: Which video file extensions are recognized?
content: The app recognizes MP4, AVI, MKV, MOV, FLV, WMV, WebM, M4V, 3GP, TS, MTS, M2TS, MPG, MPEG, VOB, and OGV video extensions.

title: Will every recognized video file play?
content: Not always. Dino USB Player can recognize many video extensions, but actual playback depends on the video encoding, audio encoding, file condition, and what your Roku device supports.

title: Why is one of my videos not listed?
content: A file may not appear if it is not recognized as a supported video extension, is hidden or inside a filtered system folder, is unreadable, or is not available from the connected USB drive.

title: Are audio, image, and subtitle files listed as videos?
content: No. The browser is focused on video playback. Audio files, image files, standalone subtitle files, folders, and unknown files are not shown as selectable video entries.

title: How are videos sorted?
content: Videos are sorted alphabetically by file name, case-insensitively. If two names match, the file path is used as a tie-breaker.

title: What does Reload Files do?
content: Reload Files returns the browser to the USB root and scans the USB drive again. Use it after connecting, replacing, or changing files on a USB drive.

title: How do I open a video?
content: Use the Roku remote D-pad to highlight a video in the USB browser, then press OK to open it in the full-screen player.

title: What playback controls are available?
content: The player includes rewind 5 seconds, play/pause/replay, forward 5 seconds, subtitles when available, and a More menu with options such as Restart, Audio Track when available, and Close Player.

title: How do I show the video controls?
content: Press OK while watching a video to show the transport overlay. The overlay auto-hides while the video is playing.

title: How do I hide the video controls?
content: Wait for the overlay to auto-hide during playback, or press Back when the overlay is visible. Pressing Back with the overlay visible hides the controls before closing the player.

title: Can I use the Roku Play button?
content: Yes. The Play remote key toggles play and pause.

title: Can I restart a video?
content: Yes. Use the Replay remote key or choose Restart from the player options. Restart resets playback to the beginning and clears saved progress for that video.

title: Does the app remember where I stopped watching?
content: Yes. Dino USB Player saves playback progress while playing, when paused, and when the player is closed, then uses that saved position when you open the video again.

title: When is saved progress cleared?
content: Saved progress is cleared when a video finishes or is restarted. The app also avoids keeping progress for very short videos, very early positions, and near-end positions.

title: How much playback progress can the app remember?
content: The app stores up to 30 playback records.

title: Can I clear playback and resume data?
content: Yes. Open Settings and use Clear Playback Data to remove stored playback and resume records.

title: Will clearing playback data delete my USB videos?
content: No. Clearing playback data only removes saved app progress records on Roku. It does not delete video files from your USB drive.

title: Which subtitle formats are supported?
content: Dino USB Player detects SRT, VTT, ASS, SSA, TTML, DFXP, and XML subtitle files stored in the same folder as videos.

title: How should subtitle files be stored?
content: Put subtitle files in the same folder as the video. Subtitle files with the same base name as the video are prioritized before other subtitle files in that folder.

title: How do I know if a video has subtitles?
content: When same-folder subtitles are detected, the USB browser can show a CC indicator in the video row metadata.

title: How do I turn subtitles on or off?
content: Use the subtitle button in the player. With one subtitle file, the button toggles subtitles on and off. With multiple subtitle files, it opens a subtitle picker that includes Turn Off Subtitles.

title: Can the app detect subtitle languages?
content: The app tries to infer subtitle languages from filenames. It recognizes common markers for English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, and Chinese.

title: Why did subtitles fail to load?
content: A subtitle may fail if the file is unreadable, damaged, unsupported by Roku playback, or not accessible from the USB drive. The player shows subtitle-load error text when applying subtitles fails.

title: What subtitle access is included for free users?
content: Free users can use subtitles for the first 20 minutes of each video when subtitle files are available. After 20 minutes, active subtitles are cleared and enabling subtitles again is blocked unless you subscribe.

title: Does restarting playback reset free subtitle access?
content: Restarting playback returns to the beginning of the video, so free users can use subtitles again within the first 20 minutes.

title: What is included for free?
content: Free users can open the first filename-sorted video from the USB browser. Videos after the first free item show a lock overlay and subscription prompt.

title: Why is a video locked?
content: Videos beyond the first free item are locked for free users. Subscribe to unlock the full USB video library.

title: What does a subscription unlock?
content: A subscription unlocks the full USB video library and extended subtitle access.

title: How do I subscribe?
content: Choose Subscribe from the app menu or from a subscription prompt. Purchases are handled through Roku.

title: How do I manage my subscription?
content: Subscribed users can open Manage Subscription in the app. You can also visit https://my.roku.com/subscriptions or manage the subscription from the Roku Home screen by highlighting Dino USB Player, pressing the * button, and selecting Manage subscription.

title: What happens after a successful purchase?
content: After a successful purchase, the app saves the Roku entitlement, refreshes subscription state, and reloads the USB browser so locked videos can unlock.

title: What happens if I cancel a purchase?
content: If you cancel during Roku checkout, the subscription screen remains available and your access level does not change.

title: Does the app recover existing Roku subscriptions?
content: Yes. Dino USB Player runs a subscription recovery flow at startup and checks Roku purchase information to restore valid subscription access when possible.

title: Does Dino USB Player need the internet?
content: USB video playback is based on your attached drive, but internet access may be needed for Roku subscription purchase and validation, Help/FAQ, Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, support links, or feedback links.

title: What happens if network connectivity is lost?
content: The app listens for Roku link-status changes and can show a No Internet progress dialog when network connectivity is lost.

title: Is Dino USB Player a cloud storage service?
content: No. Dino USB Player is a local USB video player. It is not a cloud storage, backup, or media hosting service.

title: Does the app upload my USB videos?
content: No. Dino USB Player is designed to play videos from your attached USB drive on Roku. It does not provide cloud video upload or hosting.

title: What information is shown in Settings?
content: Settings can show screen resolution, screen aspect ratio, local storage information, USB storage size when a likely external USB volume is detected, and the Clear Playback Data action.

title: Why does USB storage size not appear?
content: The app only shows USB storage size when it detects a likely external USB volume. Very small volumes below 512 MB may be treated as unlikely to be external USB storage.

title: Where can I read the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use?
content: Privacy Policy and Terms of Use are available from the app menu.

title: Where can I get support?
content: Open Support & Feedback from the app menu. The support QR code points to the Dino USB Player Facebook page.

title: Where can I send feedback or suggestions?
content: Open Support & Feedback from the app menu and use the feedback form QR code.

title: What information is shown on the About page?
content: The About page shows Dino USB Player app, developer, and version details.
